appraisal_events.evidence: quand Swann jugeait Brichot ... comme un pédant ... malgré tout le savoir de l'un
appraisal_events.explanation: Swann dismisses Brichot as a pedant despite his real erudition; the narrator flags this as the effect of Guermantes snobbery infiltrating Swann's judgment rather than a fair assessment, so the dismissal is undercut even as it is reported.

appraisal_events.evidence: l'autre comme un mufle, malgré ... tout le génie de l'autre; jamais il n'eût osé présenter ni l'un ni l'autre à la duchesse
appraisal_events.explanation: Swann dismisses Elstir as boorish despite his genius and would never dare present him to the duchess; the narrator again attributes this verdict to borrowed Guermantes esprit rather than genuine judgment, softening the diminishment with irony.

status_effects.explanation: Socially recast as merely pedantic despite genuine erudition, though the narrator's irony toward Swann's judgment tempers the diminishment.

ambiguities: M. Verdurin appears only as part of the salon-location phrase 'chez les Verdurin' and performs no action in this passage, so he was not scored.

Baron de Charlus is mentioned only as the unnamed subject of a calembour whose content is never given before the passage ends, and the duke's remarks are more evaluative of Mme de Guermantes's wit than of Charlus himself; scoring an event for Charlus here would require inventing the joke's content, so he was omitted.
